A3-MARA-OPEN.text: I gave Vane a working copy. She paid me. Now my correction is on the route she means to sell back to everyone.
No. I wanted the work to count. I didn't ask hard enough who it would count for.
Then I owe you the part I left out.
I helped maintain the Tide Ledger. That was one of our service surveys.
Years ago, an operator tried to run more channels from the centre. We changed a gate before the receiving station had confirmed its level.
A relief boat sat on the mud until the next safe tide. Nobody died. People waiting for supplies still went without them.
I had a doubtful reading. I let certainty outrank it. Afterwards I kept the chart where nobody could use it.
Until you gave it to me without telling me why it mattered.
I thought you would ask the questions I had stopped asking. I made that choice for you. I'm sorry.
I should have read what I was agreeing to, not what I hoped it meant.
Yes. And you should have had the history. Both things can be true.
Then let's stop leaving parts out.

A3-MARA-ROUTE.text: There is a service landing at Bellweather. I'll put the tracing here. Check today's water, and tell someone where you're going.
A route, a check, and someone who knows to ask. That's a better beginning.

A3-WATCH-OPEN.text: We're going to the shoal. I need someone here who knows our route and will keep the landing clear.
At last. A command appropriate to my stature.
A request. With two names on the answer.
Quibble and Fine Print. Harbour watch. Both responsible, both credited.

A3-ROUTE-OK.text: West service approach. Fixed transit. Today's ebb, not yesterday's sheltered basin.
Now the old route and the present water have had an introduction.

A3-VOYAGE.text: That arch looks less like a treasure entrance from this side.

A3-SHOAL-ARRIVE.text: Someone gave a public works station the manners of an ancient warning.
People read warnings more carefully when they look expensive.
They left a dry walkway. I like the practical part.

A3-BRAM-OPEN.text: Visitor. Nell. Mara said I should ask what you need.
Someone to read the labels before touching the things beneath them.
Then you're already ahead of the last inspection.
The company is using this station to make one paid route the dependable one. I need to know how to stop that without wrecking the harbour.
Good. Most people shorten that question in the dangerous place.

A3-INCIDENT-NOTE.text: The relief boat was stranded after a change without a receiving acknowledgement. That supports Mara's account.
It doesn't make the old operator and today's company the same people.

A3-RECORDER-SERVICE.text: Two tabs. Blue triangle. A replaceable collar.
Six in a box. Seven, if the supplier has had a good morning.
The cover is old. The catalogue is more useful.

A3-RECORD-PRINT.text: A treasure I can leave here and still take with me.

A3-RECORD-VERIFIED.text: A command, a calibration and a pending order. Enough to follow. Not permission to invent the rest.

A3-DRUM-OPEN.text: If that stops sending orders, does everything stop safely?
No. Water keeps arriving. Gates need a coordinated setting, not an absent supervisor.
So breaking it would leave the problem in charge.

A3-MODEL-SUCCESS.text: Same watch. Each local level. Every station ready before the centre lets go.
The machine was built to be maintained by people who could talk to one another.
We have been rather slow to service that part.

A3-EGG-CROWN.text: Could this be the relic the pedestal deserves?
Only if you write its part number.
Put it back. We've only just made the records legible.

A3-PLAN-READY.text: We don't need a bigger way to break the centre. We need the local stations ready to stop depending on it.
And a record of why you're doing it.
Current readings. Named people. The operating copy beside the access notices.
That sounds less like an adventure.
It sounds like one we might bring everyone home from.

A3-END.text: Instructions. And the reason nobody should carry them alone.
Home. We have people to ask, not orders to give.

lines.text: Linked gates, local signals, a central chart drum. It moves water between connected channels. Sailors gave it the rest of the ocean in the telling.

topics.question: Was Vane there when the relief boat stranded?

lines.text: Not in the work I saw. Don't put a familiar face into an old gap. The record should still say who signed what.
First to keep it from another confident operator. Later because returning it meant explaining why I'd hidden it. The second reason lasted longer.

topics.question: How do we reach the installation?

lines.text: The service landing, not the company approach. Here is my tracing. Check it against today's board; old ink doesn't know today's water.
I'll stay where stranded crews can find a door. You need someone to hear you when you return, not everyone in one boat.
You may be. You don't have to make me comfortable before we do something useful.

topics.question: We'll need more than your account.

lines.text: Yes. Ask the caretaker for the operating record. His name is Bram. Ask what he needs before deciding what he knows.
It's on the bar. Keep the original survey with it. One shows the entrance; the other gives you something to check.
I will keep this approach open.
I will keep the departure entry and take messages. Partner, not equipment.
Agreed.
Not by standing here more magnificently.
But a clear landing and an accurate message are available within our budget.
We tell Mara and keep the approach clear. We do not improvise a gate setting.

topics.question: Does their charter let them close everything?

lines.text: I'll read the whole charter before answering that. A clause without its neighbours is a dangerous pet.
Not while you're asking for useful work. I am trying not to spoil the novelty.

topics.question: Will you take me to Bellweather?

lines.text: Yes. We have a service route to check, and people ashore to tell. I would prefer not to become a second unexplained absence.
Put today's board, the fixed marks and the tracing together. I'll check your conclusion, not supply it.
West approach, fixed transit, today's ebb. I agree with what you've checked.
I do. You have my passage and my help. It is useful to say these things before someone starts naming the cabin.

topics.question: What will you do at the shoal?

lines.text: Mind the berth and the return route. You investigate. If the instructions disagree with me, bring the instructions.
Yes. No unexplained departures. It is becoming a professional principle.

topics.question: The centre can't simply be stopped.

lines.text: Then find out what takes its place.
A navigator likes a second route before the first disappears.
Whenever you're ready. The service berth will still be here if we return.

topics.question: What does the central drum actually do?

lines.text: Times and coordinates gate commands. It doesn't contain the tide. The gates still need agreed instructions when the centre stops sending them.
Because a stopped instruction isn't a safe instruction. Local stations must accept control together first.

topics.question: Mara told me about the relief boat.

lines.text: The incident binder is here. Read it beside what she remembers. An admission and a record should help each other, not replace each other.

topics.question: Do you have the company's operating record?

lines.text: Commands, acknowledgements and settings. The duplicate recorder's collar leaks; its copies blur. Its service tray is separate from the live drive. We can repair the copy path without touching a gate.

topics.question: Who ordered the old relief-run change?

lines.text: The old duty sheet names its operator. It isn't a Vane order. Today's entries have their own authorisation marks. Keep the years apart.

topics.question: Can the local stations take over?

lines.text: There is a documented procedure. Read it at the overlook, then try the disconnected board. If you understand the copy, we can discuss the original.

topics.question: Can you do this for me?

lines.text: I can service the apparatus. I can't decide what your evidence proves, or prepare people I haven't spoken to.
A machine that works looks as though nobody did anything. I have filed several very uneventful reports.
A legible record, the procedure, and your questions. Leave the gates, the originals and my kettle.

topics.question: I have a clear operating copy.

lines.text: Read what it records before deciding what it proves.
Keep the source marks attached. A useful page shouldn't lose its address.
Good. The harbour still needs current measurements, working local controls and people who have agreed to use them.

topics.question: Can you open the command floor?

lines.text: Not under the present lock. The inspection bypass is reached by the service route, but using it safely requires local cover. Access and readiness are different problems.

topics.question: Will you help when we return?

lines.text: I'll keep the record and service access in order. Tell me when the local stations are actually ready. Not when someone hopes they are.
Which settings changed, who could pass, and what they were charged. I can give you the first. The harbour must supply the others.
I can print a departure notice without predicting the return. That is an editorial improvement.

topics.question: Don't call it a treasure hunt.

lines.text: What should I call it?
An inspection.
I shall need a larger typeface.
With her agreement and the documents beside it. A confession isn't a licence to stop checking.

topics.question: Here is a verified operating copy.

lines.text: I'll keep the source with it. We still need the access notices and fees before the headline can claim the whole story.
Then she knows where the drawings meet the weather. I should have asked her sooner.

topics.question: How can local readings agree if their levels differ?

lines.text: Agree on the watch and the map, not on being identical. Different basins can have different levels at the same time.

topics.question: Can I reuse my middle inlet reading?

lines.text: As a dated observation, yes. As tomorrow's water, no. A measurement expires as an instruction before it expires as evidence.

topics.question: The model shows local control can work.

lines.text: Then we prepare the real stations. A successful model is a reason to work carefully, not to stop checking.
The public inspection route remains available. The command floor does not. Bring your questions to the appropriate side of the rail.
Because conflicting instructions do not become safer by being sincerely given.
Neither does one instruction become right by being the only one allowed.

topics.question: Your name is on the pending dispatch request.

lines.text: Yes. I have been quite public about coordinated passage.
Coordinated and exclusive aren't the same word.
We continue to disagree about their practical separation.
Not on the basis of an objection without a workable alternative.

topics.question: The historical record supports your account.

lines.text: Keep it with the account. Neither needs to stand alone.

topics.question: We must prepare the local stations.

lines.text: Then tell us what is needed. This time we decide with the information on the table.
Keep the sequence numbers. I dislike documents that arrive without their neighbours.
I will continue guarding the neighbours.
